title: The Magellanic Clouds
caption: The Magellanic Clouds above the VLT Auxiliary Telescopes, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: The Magellanic Clouds hang in the sky over the Auxiliary Telescopes that belong to ESO's Very Large Telescope at Paranal, Chile. They are two small galaxies that keep company with our own, and here they share the sky with the telescopes built to study the Universe beyond.
The Magellanic Clouds are dwarf galaxies, far smaller than the Milky Way, and they orbit around its center as satellites. Each is a separate galaxy with its own stars, gas and dust.

They can only be seen from the Southern Hemisphere, which makes them a familiar sight above Chile's observatories and an unfamiliar one to most skywatchers in the north. As close companions of the Milky Way, they give astronomers a chance to study another galaxy's stars from relatively nearby.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera at Paranal. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: The Magellanic Clouds are visible to the eye under dark skies, but a long exposure collects more light and shows them brighter and more detailed than they appear in person.
